title: When the Escarpment Sings
premise: Cyrus Eriksen, a mountain guide blacklisted from two countries, leads a small crew of misfits who salvage what the law forgot along the escarpment coast. When his old rival Maren Voss hires them to recover a sunken survey vessel—the same wreck where their mentor died and the crew swore an oath never to return—they learn the wreck holds ledgers proving a shipping consortium framed Cyrus years ago. Racing a rival salvage fleet and a monsoon that will bury the site forever, Cyrus must choose between the clean anonymity he has guarded and the justice that would cost him his crew's safety. In the end, the crew beats the fleet by one tide, and rather than sell the ledgers, they release them publicly, scattering the consortium's empire and finally letting the crew stop running.
about_author: Zephyrine Montrose is the pen name of a former expedition cook who spent eleven seasons on coastal salvage crews before turning to writing. She lives somewhere between two port towns and refuses to say which.

chapters.title: The Weight of Moving On
chapters.summary: Cyrus Eriksen's POV. The crew finishes a small salvage job on the escarpment coast and immediately decamps, as always, before anyone asks questions. Cyrus's rules are laid out: never stop, never settle, never go back. Emotional beat: weary competence masking a man who no longer remembers why he runs.

chapters.title: A Letter Smelling of Tar
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A courier delivers a job offer from Maren Voss, the rival who testified against him years ago: recover the survey vessel Kestrel before the salvage fleet Meridian claims it. The wreck is the one where their mentor Odile died and where the crew swore never to return. Emotional beat: dread dressed as curiosity.

chapters.title: The Crew Votes With Silence
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Cyrus lays out the offer at the fire. Each crew member—Tomas the diver, Ilsa the engineer, young Pim the spotter—has a private reason the Kestrel terrifies them. No one says no. Emotional beat: the terrible intimacy of a crew bound by shared grief.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa charts the monsoon's approach: they have six tides before the storm closes the wreck site for a season, and Meridian's fleet is two tides behind. She rebuilds the old dive rig from memory and spite. Emotional beat: anxiety converted into motion.

chapters.title: What Odile Taught Us
chapters.summary: Pim's POV. Pim, who never met Odile, asks about her during the coastal trek to the site. The crew's stories contradict each other, revealing how each survivor reshaped the mentor's death to bear. Emotional beat: tenderness and the unreliability of memory.

chapters.title: The Blacklist Explained
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Flashback woven into the approach: how the consortium's ledgers were used to brand Cyrus a saboteur in two countries, how Maren's testimony sealed it. He never learned what the ledgers contained. Emotional beat: old rage, freshly sharpened.

chapters.title: First Tide: The Descent
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. First dive on the Kestrel. The wreck is deeper and more broken than remembered; Tomas finds the crew quarters intact and freezes at a door he recognizes. Emotional beat: the past is not past, it is just underwater.

chapters.title: Meridian's Shadow
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Meridian's scout ship appears on the horizon, running lights illegal and hull unmarked. Ilsa rigs decoy signals to buy time and realizes the fleet knows their position—someone is feeding them information. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening like a winch.

chapters.title: The Door Tomas Wouldn't Open
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Second dive. Tomas forces himself through Odile's cabin and finds a hidden strongbox, empty, its lock freshly scratched. Someone has been here recently. Emotional beat: violation—the wreck was a grave, now it's a crime scene.

chapters.title: Maren Comes Aboard
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Maren arrives by skiff under a flag of parley, offering to split the find and revealing she hired them not for salvage but as bait to draw out Meridian, which she believes killed Odile. Emotional beat: the disorienting possibility that the traitor might be an ally.

chapters.title: Pim Sees the Signal
chapters.summary: Pim's POV. From the cliff watch, Pim spots a shore-side lamp flashing coordinates to Meridian's scout. The informant is one of their own shore contacts—the man who supplied their charts for years. Emotional beat: the ground itself becomes untrustworthy.

chapters.title: Third Tide: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Dive three reaches the hold. Cyrus recovers a sealed case of consortium ledgers—records of bribes, sunk ships, and the framing of guides who asked questions. His own name is in them. Emotional beat: vindication arriving too heavy to lift.

chapters.title: The Argument at Low Water
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The crew splits: sell the ledgers to Maren and vanish rich, or publish them and invite Meridian's full wrath. Tomas wants justice; Ilsa wants survival; Pim wants to stop being a ghost. Emotional beat: belonging tested by the cost of keeping it.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide: Cut Line
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. During the recovery dive, Meridian divers cut their guide line in the murk. Tomas and Cyrus surface three miles adrift, ledgers lashed to Tomas's chest, half-drowned. Emotional beat: trust forged under literal pressure.

chapters.title: The Informant's Name
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Confronting the shore informant, Cyrus learns Meridian didn't buy him—he sold them out first, years ago, to save his own son from a consortium debt. The blacklist was purchased, not earned. Emotional beat: pity where hatred should be.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Maren's POV (single interlude). Maren admits her testimony against Cyrus was coerced by the consortium, that she has spent a decade buying her way back to this wreck to undo it. She asks for nothing but to be there when it ends. Emotional beat: the loneliest apology ever offered.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide: The Fleet Arrives
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Meridian's full fleet anchors over the site. Ilsa's counter-plan: use the monsoon's leading squalls as cover to run the ledgers out through the escarpment's sea caves—a route only Odile ever charted. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into audacity.

chapters.title: The Caves of Odile's Charts
chapters.summary: Pim's POV. Pim navigates the flooded caves from Odile's hand-drawn charts, the crew hauling the ledgers through collapsing passages as the squall hits. Meridian's boats lose them in the storm. Emotional beat: the dead mentor guiding them one last time.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide: What the Escarpment Sings
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Climax. Cornered at the cave mouth as the monsoon makes landfall, Cyrus faces Meridian's captain and chooses publication over escape, broadcasting the ledgers' contents on the fleet's own emergency band. The escarpment's wind carries the signal to every port. Emotional beat: the moment running stops.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Storm
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The storm passes. Meridian's empire unravels as port authorities act on the broadcast; the fleet scatters. Maren turns herself in with her own testimony, clearing Cyrus's name in both countries. Emotional beat: exhausted, disbelieving relief.

chapters.title: The Crew That Stopped
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The crew, no longer blacklisted and no longer hunted, faces the strangest question of all: what now? They repair a derelict boathouse on the escarpment—not hiding this time, but choosing. Emotional beat: belonging, finally deliberate.

chapters.title: Where the Tide Comes Back
chapters.summary: Pim's POV. Epilogue. One year later, the crew runs a licensed guide service, teaching young salvagers Odile's ethics. Pim dives the Kestrel one last time and leaves a marker at her cabin door. Emotional beat: memory honored, the future open, the song of the escarpment finally at rest.
